source_units.title_raw: GENERAL PROVISIONS FOR BUILDINGS AND STRUCTURES
source_units.text_raw:
ACCESSORY BUILDINGS
No Accessory Building shall be used for human habitation except as otherwise permitted in this by-law.
The following regulations apply to Accessory Buildings on residential properties with less than four (4) Dwelling Units: Lot Area # of Accessory Buildings permitted Total Building Footprint (maximum) Height (maximum)
Minimum distance to the Side and Rear Lot Line: 1.2 m (3.9 ft) measured to the wall of the Accessory Building.
Minimum separation distance between Accessory Buildings, or between an Accessory Building and the main Building: 1.2 m (3.9 ft) measured to any projections, eaves, Decks, etc.
Accessory Buildings are prohibited from containing a basement or any below grade construction.
An Accessory Building may be Erected on any other property, but the following requirements shall apply:
Maximum Gross Floor Area: 10% of Lot Area, up to a maximum of 600 sq m (6458.4 sq ft) and the Accessory Building shall not be larger than the main Building on the Lot. Where more than one main Building on a Lot is permitted in the Zone, a larger Accessory Building may be permitted subject to the regulations of the Zone.
Location: Rear Yard or Side Yard, provided that the Accessory Building is located no closer to the Front Lot Line than the main Building, and on a Corner Lot is no closer than the Flankage Yard minimum Setback requirement.
Distance to the Side and Rear Lot Line (minimum): 1.2 m (3.9 ft) measured to the wall of the Accessory Building.
Building Height (maximum): 6.1 m (20 ft)
Separation distance between Accessory Buildings, or between an Accessory Building and the main Building (minimum): 2.4 m (8 ft) to any projection, eave, Deck, etc.
Additional requirements for Accessory Buildings are as follows:
A shared Accessory Building may be centered on the mutual Lot Line if constructed as one Building;
A boat house and/or boat dock may be built to the water’s edge, subject to the regulations of the provincial Environmental Protection Act; and
A toll booth or security booth may be Erected at the entrance of a Parking Lot.
DECKS AND OTHER PROJECTIONS INTO YARDS
A Yard shall be open and unobstructed by any Structure, except for Accessory Buildings, from the ground to the sky.
Projecting Structures as listed in the following table shall be permitted to project from a main Building into the required Yard for the specified distance, as indicated: Structure Yard in which projection is permitted Maximum projection into Yard Minimum distance from Lot Line
The Projecting Structures Table above applies to projections in any Zone, unless otherwise specified in the regulations for the Zone.
SWIMMING POOLS
A Swimming Pool maybe Erected or placed in a Side Yard or Rear Yard provided that the pool is not less than 1.83 m (6.0 ft) from the nearest Lot Line.
A Swimming Pool shall be completely surrounded with a Fence or Structure that is:
Not less than 1.83 m (6.0 ft) in Height; and
A type that would impede unauthorized passage either through, under, or over the Fence to the pool area.
Water and Sewer services shall be in accordance with the PEI Municipal Water and Sewerage Utility General Rules and Regulations.
A temporary inflatable Swimming Pool is exempt from these requirements.
FENCES
Notwithstanding any other provision of this by-law a Fence may be placed or located in a Yard.
The maximum Height for a Fence in any Zone is 2.5 m (8.2 ft), and in the Front or Flankage Yard the Height of the Fence shall not exceed:
1.0 m (3.3 ft) in the 500 Lot Area (excluding the Port Zone);
2.50 m (8.2 ft) in Employment/Industrial Zones; and
1.83 m (6.0 ft) in any other Zone.
Except for an active farm, no Fence may be electrified or incorporate barbed wire or other dangerous material in its construction.
SATELLITE DISHES
A Satellite dish larger than 61 cm (24 in.) in diameter shall not be permitted on a street-facing portion of a Building or Structure
No more than one (1) Satellite dish may be placed on the Street-facing portion of a Building or Structure.
NON-CONFORMING BUILDINGS
Where a Building has been Erected on or before the effective date of this by-law, on a Lot having less than the minimum Lot Frontage or Lot Area , or having less than the minimum Setback required by this by-law, the Building may be repaired or renovated provided that:
The repair or renovation does not further reduce the existing Setback that does not conform to this by-law, and in the case of a Demolition, a new Building is constructed within two (2) years; and
All other applicable provisions of this by-law are satisfied.
A Building or Structure shall be deemed to be existing on the effective date of this by-law if:
It was lawfully constructed or under construction on that date; or
The Building Permit for its construction was in force and effect on that date, but this clause shall not apply unless the construction commenced within twelve (12) months after the date of issue of the Permit and is completed in accordance with the Permit in a reasonable time.
If a Building that is non-conforming under the provisions of this by-law is destroyed by a fire, or is otherwise damaged by fire to an extent of 75% or more of the assessed value of the property, it shall not be rebuilt or repaired unless:
It is rebuilt or repaired in conformity with the permitted land uses of this by-law;
An applicant who loses a Building through fire or demolition can apply to seek a variance to reinstate the property as it existed prior to its removal.
The rebuilding or repair is in conformity with other requirements of this by-law insofar as is reasonable and feasible; and
The rebuilding or repair commences within six (6) months of the date of the said destruction or damage.
BUILDING HEIGHT
The maximum Height of a Building may be increased, to accommodate a Structure housing mechanical equipment on a roof if:
The Height of the Structure does not exceed 3 m (9.8 ft) in Height above the Height permitted in the applicable Zone; and
The Structure is set back from the edge of the roof by 3 m (9.8 ft) as determined by a projections upwards of the walls.
SETBACK EXEMPTIONS
No person shall Erect a Building or Structure on a Lot and have any part of the Building or Structure closer to the Front Lot Line than the minimum Front Yard Setback which is established for the Zone in which it is located, unless the proposed Building is to be located between existing Buildings on adjoining Lots on the same Block and side of the Street, and the adjacent Buildings have a reduced Front Yard Setback, in which case the minimum Front Yard Setback for the proposed Building shall be that which aligns with the front walls of the adjacent Buildings.
When the main entrance of a proposed Building is to be oriented towards the Flankage Yard, then the Rear Yard and Side Yard setbacks may be interchanged.
STREET ORIENTATION
Residential Buildings shall be oriented toward the street with front doors and windows facing the street.
All Buildings will be generally aligned with the Street.
SIGHT TRIANGLE ON CORNER LOTS
Notwithstanding any other provisions of this by-law, no Building or Structure shall be Erected on a Corner Lot within 6 m (19.7 ft) of the triangular space included between Street Lot Lines.
No Structures or vegetation shall be placed, erected, planted or maintained at a Height over 1.0 m (3.3 ft) on a Corner Lot where it may obstruct the view from a vehicle within 6 m (19.7 ft) of the point of intersection of the Street Lot Lines.
TEMPORARY STRUCTURES
A Building Permit may be issued for a temporary Structure when:
A Building or Structure is accessory to construction in progress, such as a work or construction camp, Modular Dwelling, sales or rental Office, tool or maintenance shed and scaffold.
For a Greenhouse or other seasonal Structure or Building in any Zone where it would not be permitted by this by-law for up to six (6) months.
ONE MAIN BUILDING ON A LOT
There shall be only one (1) main Building on a Lot within the R-1L, R-1S, R-1N, R-2 and R-2S Zones.
A Building shall not be constructed or placed over any Lot boundary, regardless of whether the Lots are owned by the same Owner, except as otherwise permitted in this by-law.
Where more than one main Building is permitted on a Lot, the minimum distance between Buildings shall be 6.0 m (19.7 ft).
GROUPED DWELLINGS
Grouped Dwellings are permitted on a Lot in Residential and Mixed-Use Zones, except for R-1L, R-1S, R-1N and MH, but such a grouping shall not include Single-detached Dwellings.
The City may require a Development Agreement between the Owner and the City which shall be registered on title.
The minimum distance between Buildings on any Lot containing Grouped Dwellings shall be 6.0 m (19.7 ft).
The minimum Lot Area on which Grouped Dwellings may be located shall be 0.4 hectare (1.0 acre).
The minimum standards of a Zone shall apply to any Lot on which Grouped Dwellings are located, but the minimum Lot Frontage requirement shall only apply as if one Building is being located on the Lot.
ATTACHED DWELLINGS
Attached Dwellings including Semi-detached, Townhouse, Block Townhouse and Stacked Townhouse Dwellings, must adhere to the following regulations:
A separate connection to Municipal Services shall be provided for each Dwelling Unit in accordance with the P.E.I. Municipal Water and Sewerage Utilities Rules and Regulations.
Each Dwelling Unit shall have a separate electrical service, except where sustainable Development initiatives are being utilized such as the use of a shared Windmill, ground source heat exchange system, and/or other alternative renewable energy resource.
Each Dwelling Unit shall have a separate heating device, except where sustainable Development initiatives are being utilized such as the use of a shared Windmill, ground source heat exchange system, and/or other alternative renewable energy resource.
Each Dwelling Unit shall have separate parking or access to a common Parking Lot.
UNDERGROUND WALKWAYS AND PEDWAYS
Pedestrian Pedways or tunnels that pass over or under streets are prohibited in the 500 Lot Area.
An application for an underground walkway or overhead pedways which requires an encroachment on a public Right-of-way requires:
Process for review consistent with the process for an Amendment to this by-law;
An encroachment agreement shall be signed between the registered Owner(s) of the property and the City.
A copy of the agreement shall be filed by the City in the Office of the Registrar of Deeds for the County of Queens in accordance with the provisions of the Registry Act R.S.P.E.I. 1988, Cap. R-10, and any amendments thereto, and thereupon these obligations shall be binding upon the Owner and any subsequent Owners until discharged by the agreement itself, or by the City;
The City shall reserve the right to charge an annual fee on an encroachment of a walkway over or under its Street.
FUEL-BURNING BUILDINGS
The use of fuel burning equipment in the City shall be regulated by the Environmental Protection Act R.S.P.E.I. 1988, Cap. E-9 and the Environmental Protection Act R.S.P.E.I. 1988, Cap. E-9 Air Quality Regulations (No. EC377/92).
Stand-alone biomass heating plants with less than 1 mw (megawatt) in net capacity are permitted on Employment/Industrial and Institutional properties with a minimum Lot Area of 1.5 acres, subject to all other provisions of this by-law being satisfied.
WINDMILL TOWERS
Windmills may only be permitted in the Employment/Industrial and Institutional Zones and the following additional requirements shall apply:
Windmills shall only be permitted on Lots having a minimum dimensions three (3) times the Height of the Windmill;
Windmill Height shall not exceed a total Height of 75 ft in any Zone;
All other Setback requirements shall be measured from Lot Lines to the center of the base of the Windmill and from Buildings occupied by people to the center base of the Windmill;
The Setback for Windmills shall be 1.2 times the Height of the Windmill from any property boundary or Building occupied by people on the subject Lot and 2 times the Height of the Windmill from any Building occupied by people on an adjoining Lot;
Guy wires and anchors for the Windmill shall not be located closer than one-quarter (1/4) of the Height of the Windmill to any Lot Line.
There shall be a limit of one (1) Windmill per Lot.
Roof-mounted Windmills shall not be permitted.
A Development Permit application for the Erection of a Windmill shall be accompanied by the following:
A site plan accurately drawn to scale and certified by a surveyor that shows:
The proposed location of the Windmill and the location of other Structures or Buildings;
The location and proximity of all Structures, Buildings, Utility Services on site and on adjoining properties within a radius equal to three (3) times the proposed Windmill Height;
Certification by a registered professional engineer or the manufacturer’s certification along with drawings and specifications verifying the dimensions and sizes of the various structural components of the Windmill’s construction and design data which indicates the basis of design; and,
Certified sound level values for the proposed Windmill.
One (1) Windmill may be considered in a Residential Zone as a sustainable Development initiative aimed to power a single subdivision. Such an application shall also first require that the procedures for a Minor Variances as specified in this by-law be followed and the applicant shall be required to enter into a Development Agreement upon terms and conditions acceptable to the City.
Prior to receiving a Development Permit to erect a Windmill the applicant shall receive approval from Transport Canada and comply with any Federal or Provincial Regulations pursuant to the Aeronautics Act.
A Windmill will be considered abandoned if not operated for a period of two (2) years or if it is deemed a safety hazard. Once a Windmill is deemed abandoned or a safety hazard, it shall be considered an offence of this by-law.
Climbing access to the Windmill shall be limited either by:
The installation of a Fence of not less than 1.8 m (5.9 ft) in Height with a locked gate around the Windmill base; or
By limiting Windmill climbing apparatus to no lower than 3 m (10 ft) from the ground.
ATTACHED GARAGES
An Attached Garage may be added to any dwelling, but the maximum size of the attached garage cannot exceed 40% of the gross floor area of the residential dwelling unit space.
A portion of an Attached Garage may be utilized for a Secondary Suite, subject to the Secondary Suite Regulations therein.
